parts.title: Why Does the Sun Come BACK Every Morning? (Part 1) | Cycles: Day and Night
parts.description:
Why does the Sun come back every morning? Lock in your answer from last time, then look closer at the sky from our window over two days, and at a globe and a torch: who moves, the Sun or the Earth? Be the little red dot! Part 1 of Primary 3 Science, Cycles: day and night, and what a cycle is.

In this part:
• Look closer: the sky from our window, two days speeded up
• Look closer: a globe and a torch (the Earth turns)
• Be the little red dot (one full turn of the Earth)
• What a cycle is: a repeated pattern of change
• HOLD ON! Is a pencil a cycle?
• Look closer: the traffic light
• Spot the hidden owl!

Key words: rotation, cycle, repeated pattern.
Watch Part 2: do living things have cycles too? Last episode: design a school bag like an engineer.

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies!

Why does the Sun come back every morning? P3 Science, the Cycles theme and Chapter 4, Life Cycles of Plants (pp. 73 to 75): what a cycle is, why day and night repeat, and what a life cycle is. Also fits US NGSS 1-ESS1-1 (Grade 1: patterns of the Sun) and 3-LS1-1 (Grade 3: life cycles).
Safety: never look at the Sun. In this video the Sun is a drawing, and a torch is our Sun in the model: never shine a torch at anyone's eyes. We look at the chickens and do not chase or touch them.
Try it at home: find one thing in your week that repeats like a cycle. Check it with the two questions: does it change? does it repeat? Tell someone at home.
Why cycles help: a cycle helps us predict. The Sun set tonight? It will rise tomorrow. A chick hatched? It will grow into an adult chicken.
Singapore and the US: when Singapore has day time, a child in New York, on the other side of the Earth, has nighttime. In the US, Grade 1 learns the Sun's pattern and Grade 3 learns life cycles. The science is the same: the Earth turns, and living things grow and have young.

parts.title: The Boy GREW. The Tree GREW. Why Not the TEDDY BEAR? (Part 2) | What Is a Life Cycle?
parts.description:
Long ago, on Tree Planting Day, a boy planted a young tree. His teddy bear sat beside it. Today, which ones are bigger? Look closer at then and now, follow one chick week after week, be a chick, and find out what a life cycle is and why it matters. Part 2 of Primary 3 Science, Cycles: cycles in living things.

In this part:
• Look closer: then and now (living things grow over time)
• Look closer: one chick, week after week (it grows, then it has young)
• Be a chick: from inside the egg to a new egg
• What a life cycle is
• Showdown: find the mistake in Pip's notes
• Look closer: three chickens together (why life cycles matter)
• A chant to remember it all
• Spot the hidden ladybird!

Key words: grow, reproduce, life cycle.
Watch Part 1 first! Next episode: a mango seed. What will it grow into first?
